recommendation: Keep the audit commit and do not restore the original characterization-technique wording to representation.type. Any future need for standardized characterization technique codes should be handled as a separate BRR terminology issue.
issue_request: FHIR-26940 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested that SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation.type cover either the kind of representation or the technique used to derive analytical characterization of the substance, with examples such as x-ray, HPLC, NMR, peptide mapping, and ligand binding assay.
initial_application: The request appears to have been applied in commit ae0d9e06a70438253daa330ba36e3a07a47a0d22, which changed the SubstanceDefinition spreadsheet source so representation.type included the analytical characterization technique examples requested by the Jira. The commit did not name FHIR-26940 directly, but the changed text matches the issue request.
additional_context: SubstanceDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-32115 later resolved the duplication between SubstanceDefinition.structure.technique and SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation.type by removing the characterization-technique half of representation.type. FHIR-39596 later separated characterization into SubstanceDefinition.characterization and an existing combined-branch reconciliation for FHIR-39596 removed characterization-specific remnants from the structure technique terminology. BRR minutes confirm the original FHIR-26940 approval, and no conflicting Zulip or Confluence discussion was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current source says SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation.type is only the kind of structural representation, while structure.technique and characterization.technique now carry the relevant technique concepts.
